# dsh-file-manager
A full workspace file manager that replaces the **Workspace Files** tab body in the DeepSeek Harness
(DSH) right sidebar — browse, preview, edit, create, rename, copy, move, delete, compress, extract,
upload, download, and hand files to the chat as real composer chips.
The shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-sidebar-files` tab is listing-only. This bundle registers a
replacement body and title into the **same slot keys at `priority: -10`**, so it wins over the shipp
ed entry only while this bundle is enabled. Disable the bundle and the original tab returns — nothin
g is patched or deleted.

| Plugin id | `file-manager` |
| Package | `dsh-file-manager` |
| Host half | `index.js` (4 authenti

cated Fetch routes) |
| Web half | `client.js` (no Harness client imports) |
| Node | ≥ 22 |
| Syste
m tools | `zip`, `unzip`, `tar` (only for compress/extract/download-as-zip) |
## Features

**Navigation**
- One directory at a time: the list always shows the children of the current folder,

so the breadcrumb and the rows can never disagree.
- Double-click, `Enter`, the chevron or a breadcr
umb enters a folder; `ArrowLeft` climbs to the parent; a single click only selects and never swaps t

he listing under the pointer.
- Multi-select with `Ctrl`/`Cmd` and `Shift`; the action bar appears *
*below the list**, so selecting a row never shifts the rows out from under the pointer mid-double-cl

ick.
- Search (the magnifier) is the one mode that spans folders: it filters across every directory
already loaded, keeps each hit's ancestors visible, and renders hits as an indented tree. Rows expos

e `treeitem` / `aria-level` / `data-fm-path`.
- Directories sort first, then naturally and case-inse

nsitively.
- A **jump menu** in the toolbar switches the panel to another root: the session workspac
es, the home directory, Desktop / Downloads / Documents, `/tmp` and `/`. Any absolute path works, so
the panel is not trapped inside one workspace.

**Preview and edit**
- Images, PDF, video, audio and text preview inline; other binaries fall back t

o metadata plus a download button.
- **Markdown renders as a document.** `.md`/`.markdown`/`.mdx` fi
les open through the host's own renderer — the same component the chat transcript uses — so headings
, lists, tables, task lists, block quotes and highlighted code fences look identical to a message. A
toolbar toggle switches any single file back to highlighted source; non-Markdown text keeps the sou
rce view. Relative image links resolve against the file's own directory, and a document above 200 KB

stays in the source view rather than freezing the panel.
- **HTML renders in a sandboxed frame.** `
.html`/`.htm` files open in a frame with `sandbox=""`: styles and images display, while scripts, for
ms and navigation are denied by the browser itself. Relative `src`/`href`/`poster` references are re
written to the authenticated download route against the file's own directory; root-absolute paths ar
e left alone. The same toggle flips back to highlighted source, and files above 200 KB stay in sourc

e same toggle flips back to highlighted source, and files above 200 KB stay in source view.
[该节后续省略]

Or through the plugin manager tool, which does the same thing and also records the bundle in the pro

[代码示例省略，未执行]
**From GitHub** — clone first, then add the checkout; the bundle is not published to a registry, so
the clone path is the install path:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Both forms add the dependency **and** register the bundle in the profile (`dsh.profile.bundles`), so
a restart is all that is left. `dsh plugin` without `--profile` is an error, and the profile has to
be the one you actually serve — `web` for the browser UI.
Restart the Web UI (or let HMR pick it up) and open the right sidebar → **Workspace Files**. Remove
or disable `dsh-file-manager` in the plugin list to restore the shipped tab.
## Configuration
None. There are no settings to configure.
The panel opens on the session's workspace directory and can be pointed at any other directory from
the toolbar's **More actions → Jump to** menu, which lists the session workspaces, the home director
y, Desktop / Downloads / Documents when they exist, and the usual volume roots such as `/tmp` and `/
Desktop / Downloads / Documents when they exist, and the usual volume roots such as `/tmp` and `/`.
Server-side limits:
| Limit | Value |

| JSON request body | 32 MB |
| Text file editable in the panel | 32 MB |
| Directory entries return

ed | 20000 (reported as `truncated`) |
| Upload | 8 GB |
These are guard rails against accidentally freezing the panel, not a security boundary — all of them
are generous on purpose.
## Safety model
- **Local-first by design.** DSH normally runs on the operator's own machine and these routes alread
y inherit the Host's login-cookie, Host and Origin checks, so the panel is deliberately permissive:
any existing absolute directory can be opened as the root, which is what makes it usable for a check
out, a download folder or a log directory outside the session workspace. `~` expands to the home dir
ectory, and the toolbar menu offers jump targets (workspaces, home, Desktop, Downloads, `/tmp`, `/`)

.
- Everything below that root is still confined: every relative path is normalised (empty, `.` and
`..` components are rejected, backslashes normalised, a leading `/` stripped), and a path may never

leave the root you are looking at.
- Symlink escapes are rejected: the nearest existing ancestor of

the target is `realpath`-ed and must stay inside the root.
- Uploads get unique names; writes are te
mp-file + atomic rename and compare the base mtime to surface external modification as `409 conflict

`.
- Extraction goes to a temporary directory inside the workspace and only then moves entries to a

unique destination name.
- Text/HTML/JS downloads are forced to `text/plain` + `nosniff` with `CSP:

sandbox`; only known image/PDF/audio/video types are served inline.
